classification.difficultyReason: Select radius or halve diameter, reconcile mixed units where shown, and retain exact pi in the cylinder volume.

content.prompt: Calculate the volume of these cylinders. Give your answer in exact form in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: Upright unfilled cylinder. A centre dot and rightward radius segment lie in the complete top ellipse; a downward leader from “5 m” points to the radius. Height “10 m” is rotated beside the right vertical silhouette. The lower ellipse has a red dashed rear/upper arc and solid front/lower arc. Both vertical silhouettes are solid.

Horizontal cylinder with its right circular end visible as a complete shaded ellipse. The left end is represented by its solid outer/left arc; top and bottom longitudinal silhouettes are solid. A horizontal dimension above spans the cylinder length and is labelled “14 mm”. A vertical dimension to the right spans from the top of the right ellipse to its mid-height, labelled “6 mm”; it denotes radius, not diameter. No hidden arc is drawn.

Oblique cylinder with axis rising right from a lower-left far end to an upper-right visible circular end. Curved surface is pale blue; the complete upper-right end ellipse is white. An internal double-headed radial arrow runs from approximately the end centre to the lower-right rim, labelled “7 mm”. An external double-headed dimension parallel to the axis on the lower-right side is labelled “20 mm”. Far end is shown by its solid outer arc; longitudinal silhouettes are solid. No hidden arc is drawn.

Horizontal cylinder with a complete shaded right end ellipse, solid left outer arc, and solid upper and lower longitudinal silhouettes. Label “20 m” lies below the length. A vertical double-headed dimension spans the full right-end height and is labelled “12 m”, denoting diameter. No hidden arc is drawn.

Unfilled cylinder tilted right as it rises. The upper circular end is a complete ellipse. A double-headed dimension above spans the upper end diameter, labelled “19 m”. An external double-headed dimension parallel to the right longitudinal silhouette is labelled “34 m”. Lower end is a solid outer arc; longitudinal silhouettes are solid. No hidden arc is drawn.

Upright squat cylinder with a pale-blue curved surface and a complete white top ellipse. Label “2 m” above-right has a curved leader pointing to a dashed radial segment on the top face. A vertical double-headed dimension outside the right side spans the cylinder height, labelled “2.5 m”. Vertical silhouettes and bottom outer/front arc are solid. No bottom hidden arc is drawn.

Horizontal unfilled cylinder extending right from a complete left ellipse. A centre dot and upward radius segment mark that end; a leader from “7 cm” on the left points to the radius. Label “50 cm” lies below the cylinder length. Right end has a red dashed inner/left arc and solid outer/right arc. Upper and lower longitudinal silhouettes are solid.

Short horizontal unfilled cylinder with a complete left ellipse. An internal vertical double-headed radius dimension spans approximately the centre to the bottom of the left ellipse, with “4 cm” printed to the left. A full-height vertical double-headed dimension on the right is labelled “8 cm”, giving the redundant diameter. A horizontal double-headed dimension below the cylinder is labelled “3 cm”, giving axial length. The far/right ellipse has a red dashed inner/left arc and a solid outer/right arc; longitudinal silhouettes are solid.

Upright unfilled cylinder with a complete top ellipse, centre dot and rightward radius segment. A downward leader from “10 mm” points to the radius. Height “40 mm” is rotated beside the right vertical silhouette. A horizontal double-headed dimension below spans the full cylinder width and is labelled “2 cm”, giving a redundant diameter in a different unit. Bottom ellipse has a red dashed rear/upper arc and solid front/lower arc; vertical silhouettes are solid.
